citation: Rufener L, Akre C, Rodondi P-Y, Dubois J (2024) Management of chronic non-cancer pain by primary care physicians: A qualitative study. PLoS ONE 19(7): e0307701.
summary_of_paper_topic: Swiss GPs' management of chronic non-cancer pain patients
theme_description: This theme encompasses three key components: history taking to understand patient limitations and prior treatments; looking for specific pain causes while recognizing that CNCP rarely has a single and specific cause; and exploring psychosocial dimensions including patient's interpretation of their pain and psychological factors affecting pain processing.

citation: Rufener L, Akre C, Rodondi P-Y, Dubois J (2024) Management of chronic non-cancer pain by primary care physicians: A qualitative study. PLoS ONE 19(7): e0307701.
summary_of_paper_topic: Swiss GPs' management of chronic non-cancer pain patients
theme_description: Emphasized the importance of fostering trust through continuous care and open communication. Physicians highlighted that conversations are the most important thing in managing chronic pain, requiring time to explain pain mechanisms and reassure patients while avoiding negative comments about previous treatments.

citation: Rufener L, Akre C, Rodondi P-Y, Dubois J (2024) Management of chronic non-cancer pain by primary care physicians: A qualitative study. PLoS ONE 19(7): e0307701.
summary_of_paper_topic: Swiss GPs' management of chronic non-cancer pain patients
theme_description: Addressed how socioeconomic situations (employment capacity, financial resources for treatments) and patient attitudes toward pain influenced management strategies. Insurance coverage determined treatment prioritization, with physicians sometimes recommending covered therapies over potentially more effective options.

citation: Rufener L, Akre C, Rodondi P-Y, Dubois J (2024) Management of chronic non-cancer pain by primary care physicians: A qualitative study. PLoS ONE 19(7): e0307701.
summary_of_paper_topic: Swiss GPs' management of chronic non-cancer pain patients
theme_description: Covered pharmacological approaches (non-opioid analgesics first, opioids as last resort), non-pharmacological treatments (physiotherapy, psychological support), and regular reassessment for treatment effectiveness and side effects.

citation: Payne H, Brooks SDM (2020) A qualitative study of the views of patients with medically unexplained symptoms on The BodyMind Approach: Employing embodied methods and arts practices for self-management. Frontiers in Psychology 11: 554566.
summary_of_paper_topic: MUS patients' views on embodied arts-based intervention
theme_description: Participants learned to establish linkages between body and mind through embodied practices, enabling them to monitor bodily signals and understand how emotional states influence physical symptoms.

citation: Payne H, Brooks SDM (2020) A qualitative study of the views of patients with medically unexplained symptoms on The BodyMind Approach: Employing embodied methods and arts practices for self-management. Frontiers in Psychology 11: 554566.
summary_of_paper_topic: MUS patients' views on embodied arts-based intervention
theme_description: The facilitator functioned as a catalyst, establishing safety and trust while modeling non-judgmental attitudes that encouraged participants to explore their symptoms and develop coping strategies.

citation: Payne H, Brooks SDM (2020) A qualitative study of the views of patients with medically unexplained symptoms on The BodyMind Approach: Employing embodied methods and arts practices for self-management. Frontiers in Psychology 11: 554566.
summary_of_paper_topic: MUS patients' views on embodied arts-based intervention
theme_description: Groups provided feelings of belonging, support, safety, and shared purpose, reducing isolation and fostering social cohesion essential for developing self-management confidence.

citation: Payne H, Brooks SDM (2020) A qualitative study of the views of patients with medically unexplained symptoms on The BodyMind Approach: Employing embodied methods and arts practices for self-management. Frontiers in Psychology 11: 554566.
summary_of_paper_topic: MUS patients' views on embodied arts-based intervention
theme_description: Participants reported shifts in thinking patterns and habits, lifestyle modifications, and improved mindsets that enabled them to embrace change and develop new management approaches.

citation: Payne H, Brooks SDM (2020) A qualitative study of the views of patients with medically unexplained symptoms on The BodyMind Approach: Employing embodied methods and arts practices for self-management. Frontiers in Psychology 11: 554566.
summary_of_paper_topic: MUS patients' views on embodied arts-based intervention
theme_description: The symptom transformed from being an enemy into an ally, fostering tolerance and acceptance necessary for sustainable self-management rather than seeking cure.

citation: Ashe SC, Furness PJ, Taylor SJ, Haywood-Small S, Lawson K (2017) A qualitative exploration of the experiences of living with and being treated for fibromyalgia. Health Psychology Open 4(2): 2055102917724336.
summary_of_paper_topic: Fibromyalgia patients' lived experiences and treatment
theme_description: The condition's contested medical status creates a sense of invisibility and delegitimacy. Participants felt their symptoms lacked recognition from healthcare professionals and the public, with some experiencing dismissive attitudes suggesting the condition was all in your head. This theme fundamentally influenced all remaining themes.

citation: Ashe SC, Furness PJ, Taylor SJ, Haywood-Small S, Lawson K (2017) A qualitative exploration of the experiences of living with and being treated for fibromyalgia. Health Psychology Open 4(2): 2055102917724336.
summary_of_paper_topic: Fibromyalgia patients' lived experiences and treatment
theme_description: Healthcare encounters deviated significantly from traditional medical pathways. Participants described prolonged diagnostic processes, dismissive consultations, and a perception of being mistrusted regarding pain medication requests. They noted conflicting treatment approaches and insufficient specialist knowledge among healthcare providers.

citation: Ashe SC, Furness PJ, Taylor SJ, Haywood-Small S, Lawson K (2017) A qualitative exploration of the experiences of living with and being treated for fibromyalgia. Health Psychology Open 4(2): 2055102917724336.
summary_of_paper_topic: Fibromyalgia patients' lived experiences and treatment
theme_description: Participants restructured their social connections, forming what one described as a Fibro-family with others who understood the condition. Traditional friendships often dissolved due to incomprehension, while support groups provided crucial validation and mutual understanding previously unavailable.

citation: Ashe SC, Furness PJ, Taylor SJ, Haywood-Small S, Lawson K (2017) A qualitative exploration of the experiences of living with and being treated for fibromyalgia. Health Psychology Open 4(2): 2055102917724336.
summary_of_paper_topic: Fibromyalgia patients' lived experiences and treatment
theme_description: Fibromyalgia forced occupational withdrawal or significant work modifications, undermining participants' professional identities and self-esteem. Many experienced financial strain, guilt about inability to provide for families, and stigmatization regarding disability benefits.

citation: Ashe SC, Furness PJ, Taylor SJ, Haywood-Small S, Lawson K (2017) A qualitative exploration of the experiences of living with and being treated for fibromyalgia. Health Psychology Open 4(2): 2055102917724336.
summary_of_paper_topic: Fibromyalgia patients' lived experiences and treatment
theme_description: The condition disrupted family functioning, requiring dependence on partners for daily tasks and affecting parenting capabilities. Participants experienced strain in relationships and recognized their symptoms negatively impacted children's development and emotional wellbeing.

citation: Ashe SC, Furness PJ, Taylor SJ, Haywood-Small S, Lawson K (2017) A qualitative exploration of the experiences of living with and being treated for fibromyalgia. Health Psychology Open 4(2): 2055102917724336.
summary_of_paper_topic: Fibromyalgia patients' lived experiences and treatment
theme_description: Participants described an ongoing struggle with their condition rather than genuine acceptance. They adapted through lifestyle modifications, mobility aids, and home adjustments while maintaining pragmatism despite barriers to support.

citation: Kamp KJ, Morgan H, Yoo L, Munson SA, Heitkemper MM, Levy RL (2022) Symptom management needs of patients with irritable bowel syndrome and concurrent anxiety and/or depression: A qualitative study. Journal of Advanced Nursing 79(2): 775-788.
summary_of_paper_topic: IBS patients with anxiety/depression symptom management needs
theme_name: IBS negatively impacts physical and mental well-being
theme_description: Shared experiences with distressing physical symptoms (abdominal pain, urgency, diarrhea, constipation, bloating). Bidirectional relationship between IBS symptoms and anxiety/depression. IBS symptoms disrupt normal activities of daily living. Interpersonal relationships affected by symptom perception and self-consciousness.

citation: Kamp KJ, Morgan H, Yoo L, Munson SA, Heitkemper MM, Levy RL (2022) Symptom management needs of patients with irritable bowel syndrome and concurrent anxiety and/or depression: A qualitative study. Journal of Advanced Nursing 79(2): 775-788.
summary_of_paper_topic: IBS patients with anxiety/depression symptom management needs
theme_name: A trial-and-error approach to symptom management
theme_description: Identifying strategies for managing symptoms through dietary approaches and complementary methods. Impractical and ineffective interventions that lack personalization. Multiple attempts at various interventions: what haven't I tried? reflecting frustration with ongoing symptom management.

citation: Kamp KJ, Morgan H, Yoo L, Munson SA, Heitkemper MM, Levy RL (2022) Symptom management needs of patients with irritable bowel syndrome and concurrent anxiety and/or depression: A qualitative study. Journal of Advanced Nursing 79(2): 775-788.
summary_of_paper_topic: IBS patients with anxiety/depression symptom management needs
theme_name: Challenges with healthcare professionals supporting symptom management
theme_description: Negative interactions including provider dismissal and attribution to mental health causes. Lack of nutritional expertise and support, particularly regarding dietitian access and guidance.

citation: Varinen A, Vuorio T, Kosunen E, Koskela TH (2022) Experiences of patients with fibromyalgia at a Finnish Health Centre: A qualitative study. European Journal of General Practice 28(1): 157-164.
summary_of_paper_topic: Finnish fibromyalgia patients' diagnostic experiences in primary care
theme_description: Patients experienced extended waiting periods for fibromyalgia diagnosis, often undergoing repeated tests for rheumatoid arthritis and other conditions that yielded negative results.

citation: Varinen A, Vuorio T, Kosunen E, Koskela TH (2022) Experiences of patients with fibromyalgia at a Finnish Health Centre: A qualitative study. European Journal of General Practice 28(1): 157-164.
summary_of_paper_topic: Finnish fibromyalgia patients' diagnostic experiences in primary care
theme_name: Contradictory and suspicious thoughts regarding the diagnosis
theme_description: Participants faced conflicting medical opinions, negative societal stigma, and physician hesitation about documenting the diagnosis in medical records.

citation: Varinen A, Vuorio T, Kosunen E, Koskela TH (2022) Experiences of patients with fibromyalgia at a Finnish Health Centre: A qualitative study. European Journal of General Practice 28(1): 157-164.
summary_of_paper_topic: Finnish fibromyalgia patients' diagnostic experiences in primary care
theme_name: Searching for a reason for the illness
theme_description: Patients explored potential causes including hereditary factors, psychological stressors, and physical predispositions like joint hypermobility.

citation: Varinen A, Vuorio T, Kosunen E, Koskela TH (2022) Experiences of patients with fibromyalgia at a Finnish Health Centre: A qualitative study. European Journal of General Practice 28(1): 157-164.
summary_of_paper_topic: Finnish fibromyalgia patients' diagnostic experiences in primary care
theme_description: Patients reported feeling doubted by healthcare providers and relatives due to the invisibility of fibromyalgia symptoms.

citation: Varinen A, Vuorio T, Kosunen E, Koskela TH (2022) Experiences of patients with fibromyalgia at a Finnish Health Centre: A qualitative study. European Journal of General Practice 28(1): 157-164.
summary_of_paper_topic: Finnish fibromyalgia patients' diagnostic experiences in primary care
theme_name: The importance of the doctor-patient relationship
theme_description: Continuity of care and physician familiarity with fibromyalgia treatment were essential for patient satisfaction and outcomes.

citation: Varinen A, Vuorio T, Kosunen E, Koskela TH (2022) Experiences of patients with fibromyalgia at a Finnish Health Centre: A qualitative study. European Journal of General Practice 28(1): 157-164.
summary_of_paper_topic: Finnish fibromyalgia patients' diagnostic experiences in primary care
theme_description: Patients struggled accepting a chronic condition without cure, forcing adoption of new life organizational strategies.

citation: Varinen A, Vuorio T, Kosunen E, Koskela TH (2022) Experiences of patients with fibromyalgia at a Finnish Health Centre: A qualitative study. European Journal of General Practice 28(1): 157-164.
summary_of_paper_topic: Finnish fibromyalgia patients' diagnostic experiences in primary care
theme_description: Varied patient perspectives on medication effectiveness, with exercise and meaningful daily activities recognized as beneficial.

citation: Armoogum J, Foster C, Llewellyn A, Harcourt D, McCabe C (2023) 'I think it affects every aspect of my life, really': Cancer survivors' experience of living with chronic pain after curative cancer treatment in England, UK. PLoS ONE 18(9): e0290967.
summary_of_paper_topic: Cancer survivors' chronic pain experiences post-treatment
theme_description: Survivors reported feeling unheard by healthcare professionals regarding their chronic pain. They described not being listened to when attempting to discuss their condition, and encountering skepticism about whether chronic pain after cancer treatment was genuine. Some felt healthcare providers suspected them of exaggeration or psychological distress rather than accepting their physical pain as real.

citation: Armoogum J, Foster C, Llewellyn A, Harcourt D, McCabe C (2023) 'I think it affects every aspect of my life, really': Cancer survivors' experience of living with chronic pain after curative cancer treatment in England, UK. PLoS ONE 18(9): e0290967.
summary_of_paper_topic: Cancer survivors' chronic pain experiences post-treatment
theme_description: This theme captures the profound disconnect between anticipating full recovery post-treatment and living daily in persistent pain. Survivors expected acute side effects would resolve but were unprepared for long-term consequences. The reality involved negative impacts across all life domains -- physical, emotional, social, sexual, spiritual, and financial -- with survivors describing their lives as smaller with doors shut.

citation: Armoogum J, Foster C, Llewellyn A, Harcourt D, McCabe C (2023) 'I think it affects every aspect of my life, really': Cancer survivors' experience of living with chronic pain after curative cancer treatment in England, UK. PLoS ONE 18(9): e0290967.
summary_of_paper_topic: Cancer survivors' chronic pain experiences post-treatment
theme_description: Characterized by widespread lack of knowledge about chronic pain after cancer treatment among both survivors and healthcare professionals. Participants felt uninformed about risks at diagnosis, unaware of causes or management options, and encountered providers who lacked expertise in this condition.

citation: Armoogum J, Foster C, Llewellyn A, Harcourt D, McCabe C (2023) 'I think it affects every aspect of my life, really': Cancer survivors' experience of living with chronic pain after curative cancer treatment in England, UK. PLoS ONE 18(9): e0290967.
summary_of_paper_topic: Cancer survivors' chronic pain experiences post-treatment
theme_description: Survivors described difficulty identifying and accessing support services. They reported feeling abandoned post-treatment, struggling to locate appropriate care, facing extended referral delays, traveling significant distances, and experiencing referral cycles between cancer services, pain clinics, and primary care with no clear pathway forward.

citation: Armoogum J, Foster C, Llewellyn A, Harcourt D, McCabe C (2023) 'I think it affects every aspect of my life, really': Cancer survivors' experience of living with chronic pain after curative cancer treatment in England, UK. PLoS ONE 18(9): e0290967.
summary_of_paper_topic: Cancer survivors' chronic pain experiences post-treatment
theme_description: When healthcare providers diagnosed and explained their chronic pain, survivors experienced profound relief. Receiving formal diagnosis and acknowledgment validated their experiences, reduced self-doubt about being crazy, and paradoxically made the pain more manageable despite unchanged physical symptoms.

citation: Child S, Goodwin VA, Perry MG, Gericke CA, Byng R (2015) Implementing a patient-initiated review system in rheumatoid arthritis: a qualitative evaluation. BMC Health Services Research 15: 157.
summary_of_paper_topic: Patient-initiated appointment system for rheumatoid arthritis
theme_description: Education sessions with trusted nurses helped patients understand the new system and overcome initial skepticism about being discharged from consultant lists.

citation: Child S, Goodwin VA, Perry MG, Gericke CA, Byng R (2015) Implementing a patient-initiated review system in rheumatoid arthritis: a qualitative evaluation. BMC Health Services Research 15: 157.
summary_of_paper_topic: Patient-initiated appointment system for rheumatoid arthritis
theme_description: The system enabled timely access to care when needed, eliminating wasted appointments when patients were well and reducing long waiting periods for routine check-ups.

citation: Child S, Goodwin VA, Perry MG, Gericke CA, Byng R (2015) Implementing a patient-initiated review system in rheumatoid arthritis: a qualitative evaluation. BMC Health Services Research 15: 157.
summary_of_paper_topic: Patient-initiated appointment system for rheumatoid arthritis
theme_description: Concerns emerged about suitability for all patients; some lacked ability to recognize disease deterioration or confidence to call the helpline.

citation: Child S, Goodwin VA, Perry MG, Gericke CA, Byng R (2015) Implementing a patient-initiated review system in rheumatoid arthritis: a qualitative evaluation. BMC Health Services Research 15: 157.
summary_of_paper_topic: Patient-initiated appointment system for rheumatoid arthritis
theme_name: The Everyday Challenges of Managing Change
theme_description: Implementation required organizational buy-in, team communication, workload redistribution, and clarification that changes needed management and administrative back up.

citation: Day HLS (2022) Exploring Online Peer Support Groups for Adults Experiencing Long COVID in the United Kingdom: Qualitative Interview Study. Journal of Medical Internet Research 24(5): e37674.
summary_of_paper_topic: UK long COVID patients' online peer support experiences
theme_description: Focuses on inadequate healthcare support where participants faced dismissal from healthcare professionals and turned to online groups. Also covers knowledge generation through peer sharing of therapies and management techniques.

citation: Day HLS (2022) Exploring Online Peer Support Groups for Adults Experiencing Long COVID in the United Kingdom: Qualitative Interview Study. Journal of Medical Internet Research 24(5): e37674.
summary_of_paper_topic: UK long COVID patients' online peer support experiences
theme_description: Addresses how existing support networks proved insufficient, with peers providing more attuned understanding. Additionally explores advocacy efforts where groups bringing it to light validates the condition's importance.

citation: Day HLS (2022) Exploring Online Peer Support Groups for Adults Experiencing Long COVID in the United Kingdom: Qualitative Interview Study. Journal of Medical Internet Research 24(5): e37674.
summary_of_paper_topic: UK long COVID patients' online peer support experiences
theme_description: Describes how participation varied temporally, with members engaging depending on their recovery stage, individual relevance, and emotional state, reflecting fluid involvement patterns.

citation: Day HLS (2022) Exploring Online Peer Support Groups for Adults Experiencing Long COVID in the United Kingdom: Qualitative Interview Study. Journal of Medical Internet Research 24(5): e37674.
summary_of_paper_topic: UK long COVID patients' online peer support experiences
theme_description: Examines international reach benefits and challenges, varying recovery stages among members, and administration/moderation burdens on group leaders managing large communities.

citation: Day HLS (2022) Exploring Online Peer Support Groups for Adults Experiencing Long COVID in the United Kingdom: Qualitative Interview Study. Journal of Medical Internet Research 24(5): e37674.
summary_of_paper_topic: UK long COVID patients' online peer support experiences
theme_description: Emphasizes participants joining groups to feel less alone, finding reassurance through shared symptomology, while noting potential mental health impacts -- both positive and negative -- of group engagement.

citation: Dennison L, McCloy Smith E, Bradbury K, Galea I (2016) How Do People with Multiple Sclerosis Experience Prognostic Uncertainty and Prognosis Communication? A Qualitative Study. PLoS ONE 11(7): e0158982.
summary_of_paper_topic: MS patients' experiences of prognostic uncertainty
theme_description: Participants reported minimal opportunities to discuss prognosis with healthcare professionals. Negative communication experiences during diagnosis persisted emotionally over time, creating negative expectations of future interactions. MS nurses were perceived as better communicators than neurologists, though not universally available.

citation: Dennison L, McCloy Smith E, Bradbury K, Galea I (2016) How Do People with Multiple Sclerosis Experience Prognostic Uncertainty and Prognosis Communication? A Qualitative Study. PLoS ONE 11(7): e0158982.
summary_of_paper_topic: MS patients' experiences of prognostic uncertainty
theme_description: Participants demonstrated comprehension of MS's inherent variability and accepted that healthcare providers could not predict individual disease trajectories. Many held philosophical stances toward accepting life's unpredictability rooted in religious beliefs or psychological therapy.

citation: Dennison L, McCloy Smith E, Bradbury K, Galea I (2016) How Do People with Multiple Sclerosis Experience Prognostic Uncertainty and Prognosis Communication? A Qualitative Study. PLoS ONE 11(7): e0158982.
summary_of_paper_topic: MS patients' experiences of prognostic uncertainty
theme_description: A widespread coping strategy involved focusing on daily life rather than the uncertain future. Participants described living one day at a time or avoiding future-oriented thinking, though intrusive worries about disability and dependence frequently interrupted this approach.

citation: Dennison L, McCloy Smith E, Bradbury K, Galea I (2016) How Do People with Multiple Sclerosis Experience Prognostic Uncertainty and Prognosis Communication? A Qualitative Study. PLoS ONE 11(7): e0158982.
summary_of_paper_topic: MS patients' experiences of prognostic uncertainty
theme_name: Forming and editing personal beliefs about prognosis
theme_description: Despite acknowledging uncertainty, participants developed specific beliefs about their disease trajectory through multiple sources: salient personal experiences with other MS patients, healthcare provider communication, internet research, and their own disease experiences over time.

citation: Dennison L, McCloy Smith E, Bradbury K, Galea I (2016) How Do People with Multiple Sclerosis Experience Prognostic Uncertainty and Prognosis Communication? A Qualitative Study. PLoS ONE 11(7): e0158982.
summary_of_paper_topic: MS patients' experiences of prognostic uncertainty
theme_description: Participants expressed conflicting feelings about receiving detailed prognosis predictions. Primary concerns included hopelessness from negative information and uncertainty about information's practical usefulness when no curative treatments exist.

citation: Dennison L, McCloy Smith E, Bradbury K, Galea I (2016) How Do People with Multiple Sclerosis Experience Prognostic Uncertainty and Prognosis Communication? A Qualitative Study. PLoS ONE 11(7): e0158982.
summary_of_paper_topic: MS patients' experiences of prognostic uncertainty
theme_description: Participants emphasized that prognosis discussions require careful timing (inappropriate at diagnosis), face-to-face delivery, healthcare provider expertise combined with supportive skills, and integration within comprehensive care plans addressing emotional wellbeing alongside medical management.

citation: Bukhsh A, Goh B-H, Zimbudzi E, Lo C, Aksber N, Khan TM (2020) Type 2 Diabetes Patients' Perspectives, Experiences, and Barriers Toward Diabetes-Related Self-Care: A Qualitative Study From Pakistan. Frontiers in Endocrinology 11: 534873.
summary_of_paper_topic: Pakistani T2DM patients' self-care perspectives and barriers
theme_description: Family members serve as critical support systems, assisting with medicine identification and administration, glucometer operation, hypoglycemia symptom recognition, and initial diabetes diagnosis awareness. However, social gatherings present dietary adherence challenges as culturally unsuitable foods dominate, and patients occasionally skip medications during family events.

citation: Bukhsh A, Goh B-H, Zimbudzi E, Lo C, Aksber N, Khan TM (2020) Type 2 Diabetes Patients' Perspectives, Experiences, and Barriers Toward Diabetes-Related Self-Care: A Qualitative Study From Pakistan. Frontiers in Endocrinology 11: 534873.
summary_of_paper_topic: Pakistani T2DM patients' self-care perspectives and barriers
theme_description: Physician counseling significantly influences medication adherence, exercise adoption, and dietary modification understanding. Yet variable experiences emerged -- some received comprehensive education on hypoglycemia management while others received minimal guidance. Patients attended appointments irregularly, primarily seeking free medicines or addressing emergencies rather than routine checkups.

citation: Bukhsh A, Goh B-H, Zimbudzi E, Lo C, Aksber N, Khan TM (2020) Type 2 Diabetes Patients' Perspectives, Experiences, and Barriers Toward Diabetes-Related Self-Care: A Qualitative Study From Pakistan. Frontiers in Endocrinology 11: 534873.
summary_of_paper_topic: Pakistani T2DM patients' self-care perspectives and barriers
theme_description: Family and friends served as primary information sources. Participants harbored misconceptions about diabetes curability and etiology, attributing causes to herbal medicine use, depression, or medication side effects. Symptomatic presentations like frequent urination and fatigue initially drove healthcare visits.

citation: Bukhsh A, Goh B-H, Zimbudzi E, Lo C, Aksber N, Khan TM (2020) Type 2 Diabetes Patients' Perspectives, Experiences, and Barriers Toward Diabetes-Related Self-Care: A Qualitative Study From Pakistan. Frontiers in Endocrinology 11: 534873.
summary_of_paper_topic: Pakistani T2DM patients' self-care perspectives and barriers
theme_name: Complications of Diabetes and Other Comorbidities
theme_description: Fear of diabetes complications motivated strict medication adherence. Simultaneously, comorbidities including joint pain, fatigue, and heart problems significantly restricted physical activity engagement and exercise sustainability.

citation: Bukhsh A, Goh B-H, Zimbudzi E, Lo C, Aksber N, Khan TM (2020) Type 2 Diabetes Patients' Perspectives, Experiences, and Barriers Toward Diabetes-Related Self-Care: A Qualitative Study From Pakistan. Frontiers in Endocrinology 11: 534873.
summary_of_paper_topic: Pakistani T2DM patients' self-care perspectives and barriers
theme_description: Food cravings, needle phobia, forgetfulness, and medicine non-adherence emerged as personal behavioral barriers. Psychological resistance to dietary restrictions and injection-related anxiety compromised self-management consistency.

citation: Bukhsh A, Goh B-H, Zimbudzi E, Lo C, Aksber N, Khan TM (2020) Type 2 Diabetes Patients' Perspectives, Experiences, and Barriers Toward Diabetes-Related Self-Care: A Qualitative Study From Pakistan. Frontiers in Endocrinology 11: 534873.
summary_of_paper_topic: Pakistani T2DM patients' self-care perspectives and barriers
theme_description: Financial constraints limiting healthy food affordability, hectic work schedules preventing exercise incorporation, weather extremes disrupting physical activity, and household responsibilities substituting perceived exercise needs created systemic obstacles to recommended self-care practices.

citation: Roikjaer SG, Simony CP, Timm HU (2020) Qualitative study to explore what patients with heart failure find significant during integrated palliative care sessions in a Danish clinic. BMJ Open 10(12): e043955.
summary_of_paper_topic: Heart failure patients' experiences of integrated palliative care
theme_description: Patients perceived the integrated sessions as addressing their concerns regardless of type. Participants felt cared about, which enabled them to share personal experiences, thoughts or worries and experienced relief from physical, psychosocial, and existential problems.

citation: Roikjaer SG, Simony CP, Timm HU (2020) Qualitative study to explore what patients with heart failure find significant during integrated palliative care sessions in a Danish clinic. BMJ Open 10(12): e043955.
summary_of_paper_topic: Heart failure patients' experiences of integrated palliative care
theme_name: Telling Your Story Provides a Sense of Meaningfulness
theme_description: The narrative approach created genuine interest in patients' lived experiences. Patients interpreted this as genuine interest from the professionals and generated coherence by helping them recognize the bigger picture, thereby creating a sense of meaning.

citation: Roikjaer SG, Simony CP, Timm HU (2020) Qualitative study to explore what patients with heart failure find significant during integrated palliative care sessions in a Danish clinic. BMJ Open 10(12): e043955.
summary_of_paper_topic: Heart failure patients' experiences of integrated palliative care
theme_name: Integrating Perspectives of Heart Failure Into Everyday Life
theme_description: Patients combined embodied understanding with medical knowledge. This integration allowed participants to balance worries with hope and living life while comprehending both physiological aspects and existential implications of their diagnosis.

citation: Lightbourne A, Foley S, Dempsey M, Cronin M (2023) Living with endometriosis: A reflexive thematic analysis examining women's experiences with the Irish healthcare services. Qualitative Health Research 34(4): 311-322.
summary_of_paper_topic: Women's experiences navigating Irish healthcare for endometriosis
theme_description: Healthcare providers minimized women's symptomatology by treating severe pain as typical. Participants recalled being told to embrace feeling unwell or that bad periods are normal. This dismissal occurred at both pre-diagnosis and post-diagnosis stages, undermining patients' lived experiences.

citation: Lightbourne A, Foley S, Dempsey M, Cronin M (2023) Living with endometriosis: A reflexive thematic analysis examining women's experiences with the Irish healthcare services. Qualitative Health Research 34(4): 311-322.
summary_of_paper_topic: Women's experiences navigating Irish healthcare for endometriosis
theme_description: Participants reported systemic failures across all healthcare levels -- general practice through aftercare. Women described lacking support and information regarding symptom management. The public healthcare system was deemed unsuitable, prompting some to seek treatment abroad.

citation: Lightbourne A, Foley S, Dempsey M, Cronin M (2023) Living with endometriosis: A reflexive thematic analysis examining women's experiences with the Irish healthcare services. Qualitative Health Research 34(4): 311-322.
summary_of_paper_topic: Women's experiences navigating Irish healthcare for endometriosis
theme_description: Diagnostic delays ranged from 2-32 years (average 6-7 years). Extended waiting periods caused psychological distress, financial burden, and fertility concerns. One woman reported suffering seven years before formal acknowledgment of her condition.

citation: Lightbourne A, Foley S, Dempsey M, Cronin M (2023) Living with endometriosis: A reflexive thematic analysis examining women's experiences with the Irish healthcare services. Qualitative Health Research 34(4): 311-322.
summary_of_paper_topic: Women's experiences navigating Irish healthcare for endometriosis
theme_description: Healthcare professionals and the general public demonstrated insufficient knowledge about endometriosis. Women felt obligated to self-educate and self-advocate. Medical professionals should recognize classic endometriosis symptoms earlier in primary care settings.

citation: Lightbourne A, Foley S, Dempsey M, Cronin M (2023) Living with endometriosis: A reflexive thematic analysis examining women's experiences with the Irish healthcare services. Qualitative Health Research 34(4): 311-322.
summary_of_paper_topic: Women's experiences navigating Irish healthcare for endometriosis
theme_name: Navigating Ignorance, Taboo and Societal Views
theme_description: Limited specialist services created broader cultural impacts affecting relationships, workplace experiences, and social understanding. Women faced difficulty disclosing diagnoses and experienced career consequences from healthcare access needs.

citation: Moore C, Cogan N, Williams L (2023) A qualitative investigation into the role of illness perceptions in endometriosis-related quality of life. Journal of Health Psychology 28(12): 1157-1171.
summary_of_paper_topic: Illness perceptions and quality of life in endometriosis
theme_description: This theme captures how endometriosis prevents participants from living the life they wanted and creates a sense that their potential remains unrealized. The theme encompasses disruptions across multiple life domains -- education, work, relationships, and daily functioning. Participants expressed feeling powerless, describing endometriosis as controlling their lives.

citation: Moore C, Cogan N, Williams L (2023) A qualitative investigation into the role of illness perceptions in endometriosis-related quality of life. Journal of Health Psychology 28(12): 1157-1171.
summary_of_paper_topic: Illness perceptions and quality of life in endometriosis
theme_description: Participants perceived their identity as fundamentally altered by endometriosis. Many described feeling like a different person or experiencing a lost sense of self. The theme explores how symptoms eroded previously salient identity aspects, particularly femininity and sexual identity. Participants faced invalidation from healthcare providers, leading to self-doubt.

citation: Moore C, Cogan N, Williams L (2023) A qualitative investigation into the role of illness perceptions in endometriosis-related quality of life. Journal of Health Psychology 28(12): 1157-1171.
summary_of_paper_topic: Illness perceptions and quality of life in endometriosis
theme_description: This theme presents two contrasting emotional dimensions. First, endometriosis functions as an emotional burden, generating frustration, anger, sadness, guilt, and loneliness. Second, some participants found emotional strength through establishing coping mechanisms and supporting others, deriving empowerment and pride from their experiences.

citation: Patel K, Tchanturia K, Harrison A (2016) An Exploration of Social Functioning in Young People with Eating Disorders: A Qualitative Study. PLoS ONE 11(7): e0159910.
summary_of_paper_topic: Social functioning in adolescents with eating disorders
theme_description: Comprising subordinate themes of friendships dissolving (patients reported losing friends or lacking social connections), interpersonal adversity (teasing, bullying, competitiveness), and impoverished social networks resulting from illness and hospitalization.

citation: Patel K, Tchanturia K, Harrison A (2016) An Exploration of Social Functioning in Young People with Eating Disorders: A Qualitative Study. PLoS ONE 11(7): e0159910.
